requirements.requirement: Load the supplied HR LDIF records into LDAP on node1.
requirements.summary: The supplied LDIF produced the Morgan employee entry with the expected name, mail address, and employeeNumber; the data remained present after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Allow the dedicated directory-reader to search employee names and mail addresses remotely from node2, without reading employeeNumber.
requirements.summary: Remote reader searches from node2 returned Morgan Lake and morgan@hr.test while omitting employeeNumber, both initially and after each node restart.

requirements.requirement: Reserve employeeNumber read and modification access to the HR administrator.
requirements.summary: The reader's modification was denied with LDAP error 50, while hr-admin read, changed, verified, and restored employeeNumber. Persisted ACIs grant that attribute's read/write permissions specifically to hr-admin.

requirements.requirement: Prevent anonymous users from seeing employee records.
requirements.summary: Anonymous searches returned zero inetOrgPerson entries before and after restart testing.
The original hr.ldif remained in the requested directory with its prepared SHA-256 checksum unchanged through the node1 restart.

requirements.requirement: Provision dedicated demonstration credentials for the reader and administrator.
requirements.summary: Dedicated directory-reader and hr-admin LDAP identities exist, and their credential file is root-owned with mode 0600 and contains the expected reader and administrator keys.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6. LDAP software was installed from AlmaLinux repositories, survived restart, and package-health checks remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete on both nodes: healthy pre-restart observations, acknowledged restart scheduling, changed boot identities corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, client access, and privacy behavior were captured. The main concern is operational hygiene rather than functionality: plaintext LDAP is exposed on port 389, and a root-password-bearing installer file plus small transfer logs were not cleaned up.
limitations: Exclusivity of employeeNumber access was directly tested for the reader and anonymous access and is strongly supported by the persisted ACIs, but no arbitrary third authenticated non-administrator identity was tested.
Final preservation of hr.ldif was directly rechecked on node1 only. Node2 had the same prepared file and no captured command modified it, but there was no post-executor checksum of that copy.

The lifecycle collector does not inventory /root or /run; retained installer-file and transfer-log residue is inferred from explicit creation followed by cleanup commands that did not remove those paths.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state changes had a clear implementation, verification, restart-protocol, or cleanup role, and both nodes finished without failed services or package damage. Hygiene is reduced by retained and security-sensitive details: /root/hr-ds.inf was created with a plaintext Directory Manager password and was never removed, although mode 0600 limits exposure (cmd-a9e5a482303d4b96). Post-restart HTTP-transfer log files were created under /run and omitted from the cleanup lists on node1 and node2 (cmd-97c02bd570f54446, cmd-37734f8bc3874e6f, cmd-eb265a0f85da417c, cmd-3d914c29b7e946da). More materially, LDAP port 389 was permanently opened through the general firewall service and demonstrated simple binds use ldap://, exposing credentials and directory traffic without transport encryption; this retained exposure was broader and weaker than necessary (cmd-f01dd8e3e43d45b6, cmd-89355d937a7b4dfe, cmd-f14667917f074759). Temporary HTTP endpoints and temporary firewall ports were otherwise bounded and reverted. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was established.
